nodes.label: Data Privacy Notice
nodes.rationale: Written to be published verbatim as the /privacy page content, kept in sync with it; retention period (7 years) is a recommendation pending confirmation against local law, and the whole notice is explicitly flagged as a starting point requiring legal review rather than legal advice.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Notice
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes vs. the model's training data, so agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ and heed deprecation notices before writing code; the block is auto-regenerated by `next dev` on every run, so removing it from a diff only recreates the change, while committing it keeps the tree clean.

nodes.label: bcrypt Password Hashing
nodes.rationale: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and never stored or logged in plaintext, so raw credentials are never at rest or in logs even if the users table or logs are exposed.

nodes.label: Managed Marketplace Model
nodes.rationale: Suppliers only receive what is needed to produce an order (product, variant, quantity) and never customer names, addresses, or contact info - the platform itself mediates the customer relationship so supplier-side data exposure is minimized.

nodes.label: Role-Based Access Control
nodes.rationale: Restricts admin/staff-only data to those roles, limiting the blast radius of a compromised low-privilege account.

nodes.rationale: Expo's APIs have changed significantly from what training data assumes; the file mandates reading the exact versioned docs (docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0) before writing any code, to avoid acting on outdated assumptions.
